correctness.rationale: Exact reduction of the operator norm to prefix steps uses the constant-preserving linearity of inverse-shuffle expectation and an exact l1 difference basis. Each realized prefix has at most 2a-1 jumps, providing a global upper bound. Quarter-packet probes and simultaneous Hoeffding concentration for independent label indicators give an explicit matching lower bound uniformly for every fixed positive packet law. The exact finite n=2..7 table follows from a complete binomial double sum, with an independent assignment enumeration in check.py. The composition and collision arguments yield fixed-r amplification 2a^r-1 and fixed-n decay. The proof covers all stated quantifiers; finite checks are not used to infer infinite limits.

originality.rationale: The shuffle model, composition law and full one-card transition entries are acknowledged as prior. The inspected sources concern mixing distances, spectra, distribution and permutation statistics; no direct sharp adjacent-coordinate BV theorem or bias-universal large-deck norm 2a-1 was identified. The novel mechanism is a packet-run upper bound matched by concentration of alternating probes, plus exact seven-site onset. Priority remains provisional where potentially relevant dynamical-system full text was inaccessible.
residual_risks: Lalley (1999) related shuffle dynamical-system full text was not accessible for complete comparison; abstract alone cannot establish noncoverage.
Berechet (2001) and other BV-transfer-operator literature may contain an unindexed equivalent after nontrivial reformulation.

Existing explicit one-card transition matrices algebraically contain every finite-dimension coefficient; the research contribution is the sharp universal asymptotic and its stability mechanism, not the matrix entries.

value.rationale: Classifies the sharp large-deck spatial-BV norm of a natural random-permutation average uniformly over every positive packet bias at each fixed packet count. Quantifies how packet boundaries force instability and establishes an exact first finite-deck loss of nonexpansivity at seven sites. Noncommuting deck-size and shuffle-count limits distinguish variation stability from classical mixing, providing a concrete nonnormal transient phenomenon despite fixed-deck asymptotic averaging.
